options.B: Ambient air pressure changes completely neutralize all lung sounds
options.C: Paramedics are required to wear heavy noise-cancelling helmets
options.D: Stethoscopes automatically malfunction in the presence of vehicle batteries

explanation: High ambient noise and constant motion make traditional stethoscope auscultation unreliable during transit. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h3)

question: What core toxicological principle states that virtually any substance can become harmful if taken in a large enough quantity?

options.A: The first-pass elimination law
options.B: The systemic clearance threshold
options.C: The dose makes the poison principle
options.D: The bioaccumulation constant

explanation: Toxicology relies on the foundational concept that toxicity is directly related to the concentration and amount of a substance entering the body. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of a research report in the nursing profession?

options.A: To bridge the gap between clinical inquiry and evidence-based practice
options.B: To document disciplinary actions taken against staff members
options.C: To replace hospital policy manuals with academic literature
options.D: To fulfill a mandatory graduation requirement for student nurses

explanation: Research reports translate systematic investigations into actionable evidence that improves patient care outcomes in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h1)

question: How many times should a nurse compare the medication label against the prescription order?

options.A: Four times to be completely safe
options.B: Three separate times
options.C: Only once at the bedside
options.D: Twice during preparation

explanation: Checking the drug against the order upon retrieval, during preparation, and at the bedside catches discrepancies early. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h2)
